facts.value: Declared s32 (void* xfb_out_ptr, void* xfb_cur_ptr). The first pointer must address two readable/writable 32-bit slots; the second must be writable when last_draw != -1 and is read/write during fallback. Slots can retain caller values when no scan writes them. Return is 0, 1 or 2 by the final branch tests, not a guarantee that this many nonzero distinct buffers were found.

facts.value: Waits for the video flush helper, saves the last-drawn buffer when available, and scans for up to two other configured XFB addresses. It can transfer the saved current address into primary slot zero. The wait helper returns immediately with fewer than two configured XFBs; output validity also depends on caller storage initialization.

facts.value: For >=2 configured XFBs, the wait helper busy-waits while WAITDONE, DRAWDONE or NEXT records remain; for fewer it returns immediately. Selection skips last_draw and starts the second scan after the first stop index. Output slots are not pre-cleared here. A last_draw != -1 dereferences xfb_cur before the later NULL fallback check. A zero first slot with NULL current pointer returns 0; otherwise returns 2 if slot one is nonzero, else 1, even if fallback transferred zero. The known caller pre-zeroes storage.

facts.value: Initialization clears the first 0x24 bytes of its 0x28-byte state while preserving x24, stores and zeroes caller-owned storage, and registers fn_80393C14. With stdout interception installed by HSD_LogInit, incoming bytes flow to the ring and length trailers. Seek and read operations maintain a shared history cursor consumed by debug-console drawing and address parsing. The separate XFB helper supplies display-buffer slots.

facts.value: The initialized flag x0_b0 gates seek, relative movement and byte reads; x0_b1 separately tracks report capture and disabling capture leaves history readable. The coordinate getter is unconditional. Absolute traversal checks prior distance against capacity and can end beyond it; reads reject distance > capacity. Positive relative movement leaves cached line length unchanged, and zero-row movement is ignored only in the in-range branch. Capture has no zero-capacity guard. Zero read results can also be stored NUL bytes.
